decisions.reason: The frozen L7 citation to completeness did not supply sequential compactness. Current L7 correctly uses the choice-free compactness implications (clauses 1 and 3), topology agreement and the Cauchy/subsequence lemma; proper sublevels trap the Cauchy tail, giving completeness of h-prime and Hopf-Rinow compactness componentwise. Reconciled the stale L7 owning-contract citations with these exact suppliers. The carrier already differed from the assignment on arrival; no new theorem text was needed.

Chronology openness appears in justified_by, not deps. SCHEMA expressly permits this well-definedness discharge when the lemma depends on the definition. Its openness proof uses local cones, restricted timelike arcs and transitivity, rather than the derived properties of future sets; its closure clause uses only the defining predicate. The logical prerequisite graph is therefore acyclic. The short-segment and closure arguments in the definition are sound under the declared AC_omega/DC assumptions; no edit.

The frozen title said radius although the statement and proof concern its square. The current title explicitly says squared Euclidean radius. The operator-norm geodesic estimate f-double-prime >= 2(1-Gamma-norm times radius)|velocity|^2 and convex chord bound prove containment, without claiming convexity of the unsquared norm. This existing title repair resolves the overstatement; the Statement remains unchanged.

The missing chart centering in the frozen proof is an omitted routine translation, now explicit in L5 and Step 1.2. The block derivative (u,w) maps to (u,u+w), the inverse-function domain admits an exact smaller coordinate/velocity product, its open image contains a closed sufficiently small endpoint product, and the derivative bound there gives the uniform Lipschitz estimate. The current centering repair preserves all claims and adds no choice assumption.

The frozen L2 supplier requires an absolute derivative bound and cannot supply the stated one-sided reciprocal estimate. Current L2 integrates the smooth reciprocal derivative using thm-ftc-second-part. Uniqueness prevents a nonconstant geodesic velocity from vanishing; integration gives w <= 4v0/3, velocity change <= 4v0/9 and the stronger displacement bound 7v0 delta/9. The two admissible-delta cases prove v0 < 4r. Updated the stale L2 contract citation to the FTC supplier; no new item text was necessary.

The frozen strict-convex-normal clause omitted convex normality, which the supplied definition must retain. Current clause (b) explicitly requires convex normality before closure-endpoint uniqueness. Consulted Minguzzi Definition 2.3 and the adjacent Definitions 2.2 and 2.5, pp. 26-27; the current open star-shaped inverse domains, terminal position vector, signed displacement and equal-endpoint exception agree with that convention. Existing corrected Definition is retained.

The theorem fixes an arbitrary base p in C. Step 1.1 proves containment for every such base using the initial-cone supplier, so Step 2.2 legitimately instantiates it at q for the return subarc. The two opposite oriented geodesics between distinct p,q contradict uniqueness. Smooth joint inverse regularity is supplied by the every-pair inverse-function argument of the position-vector lemma L4. Null level-set derivative, punctured radial normalization, integrable-tail limit and both equality directions are sound with AC_omega/DC. No edit.

The rejected L2 citation named only the position-vector statement, which asserts smoothness of D-squared. Current L2 identifies the exact every-pair proof in that supplier Fact L4: an invertible fiber differential makes the joint differential invertible, nearby geodesics stay in the open convex set, and uniqueness identifies the inverse. Fixed compact inverse branches then control every independently chosen normal-ball inverse by the first-exit argument. Secant speeds converge at Lebesgue points; Fatou applied to Cw_N-f_N proves the refined sums, then fixed partitions give upper semicontinuity. This existing citation repair supplies the needed regularity without changing the Statement.

The rejected orientation criterion from positive coordinate time alone is false in a tilted chart. Current L5 first requires membership in the closed future cone, and Step 6.1 obtains that membership as a limit of positive scaled future radial velocities; positive time component proves only nonvanishing. The buffered chart qualifier in (a3) supplies the uniform h-component bound required for noncollapse. Compact-ball extraction, the absolutely continuous inverse-arclength proof and eventual-domain diagonal extraction give the claimed causal and inextendible limits. Existing repairs retained.

The unrescaled observer metric need not be complete (on the open flat slab it is Euclidean), so the rejected metric identification cannot supply compact-ball extraction. Current Statement explicitly denotes the complete conformal h-prime by h and uses it for all lengths and distances, componentwise. Common-domain bounded limits retain the cone and positive chart-time lower bound; zero lengths collapse; nested half-line subsequences give both tails and the weak closure relation. Added the missing L4 contract citation to the actual completeness supplier.

The rejected causal criterion excluded pure-time timelike vectors by requiring positive spatial norm, but that extra restriction is unnecessary and false. Current L1 correctly requires v0 >= spatial norm for a nonzero vector. The two leg velocities (1,+/-1,0,0) are null, their sum (2,0,0,0) is timelike and its straight path proves chronology. The parallel sum remains null. The separate timelike certificate has spatial speed at most pi/4 < 1. Existing correction retains the Example and proof conclusions.

Selecting one epsilon for every point of an arbitrary compact set would exceed the declared countable/dependent choice assumptions. Current Step 5.1 instead uses the definable family of all admissible timelike segment parameters and takes a finite subcover, with only finite choice of representatives. Compact diamonds and the strong-causality length bound establish closedness before compact truncated cones. The current Remark also correctly limits this to the forward implication; closedness and compact cones alone allow closed timelike curves.

Choosing U=M cannot contradict strong causality. Current L1 chooses U=M minus an image point y distinct from the loop base x. Every V containing x and contained in U then has a causal segment with endpoints in V that exits U, proving the needed contradiction. Closed causal cones, chronology openness and null achronal boundaries give almost-everywhere indicator convergence and dominated convergence; the intermediate timelike point has a positive-measure open separation from the earlier closed cone. Existing proof correction retained.

Completeness of the unrescaled observer metric was an unsupported premise. Current L5 explicitly fixes the complete conformal h-prime for every auxiliary length and distance. A finite total length in a compact diamond makes a cofinal sequence Cauchy in that same complete component and the entire tail convergent, contradicting inextendibility. Continuity from above then gives future-volume decay; monotonic positive past volume gives logarithmic divergence. Open cone differences prove strict causal monotonicity and unique Cauchy-level crossings. Existing correction retained.

The rejected strict inequality for J-minus(S_b) wrongly removed its reflexive level. Current L1 correctly uses t <= b, so p belongs to the compact truncated cone K. Shrinking through compact chart balls gives the prescribed diameter and enclosing normal neighborhood; a first-exit subsequence and acausality force the boundary limit to p, a contradiction. The future-branch flat cone function is smooth at the vertex, its positive gradient is past timelike, and the finite-ball cutoff construction proves a neighborhood plateau on K. Existing repair retained.

The Euclidean supplier guarantees a plateau on a compact set, not on its neighborhood. Current L5 first thickens K to a finite union K1 of closed balls inside the open support domain, with K in Int(K1), and applies the supplier to K1. Step 4.1 selects a precompact ball enclosing the explicit truncated cone and uses this neighborhood plateau. The future branch avoids the unwanted past cone; flatness gives smoothness at the null boundary and vertex, and grad(Q)=-2v gives the required past-timelike gradient. Existing local repair retained.

The rejected scope note assigned local causality to a theorem that supplies only convex normal neighborhoods. Current note separately cites thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone for local causal calculus and explicitly identifies completeness as that of X=grad(T)/g(grad(T),grad(T)), preserving the distinction from the genuine gradient. Mathematical model deductions, optional physical interpretations and empirical nonclaims remain separate. Existing citation/terminology repairs retained; owning-page summaries still require reconciliation.

The slab supplier asserts only the half-time Cauchy slice. Current Step 1.1 proves every slice directly: strict time monotonicity and spatial Lipschitz increments give an interior point limit if either endpoint time lies in (0,1), contradicting inextendibility. Thus the time range is (0,1) and every slice is met once. The gradient is -partial_0, its normalized field is partial_0 and its maximal domain through half-time is (-1/2,1/2), refuting completeness. Existing added proof and suppliers are adequate.

The rejected every-slice premise is not supplied by the half-time slab theorem. Current Step 2.1 independently derives the full (0,1) time range from flat spatial Lipschitz increments, Euclidean completeness and no-endpoint inextendibility, hence every rational-T level is Cauchy. T-prime=(1-t)^(-2)+t^(-2)>0, T has range R and T(1/2)=0. Its inverse gives a global flow for X=partial_0/T-prime; beta=1/T-prime^2 gives the orthogonal product. The current Example and summary correctly specify the normalized field, not grad(T). Existing repairs retained.

ledger_updates.evidence: L2 restates the chart-time estimate for any dominated cone chart, whereas revised basic-limit clause (a3) requires a coordinate ball compactly contained in a larger adapted chart. Step 1.1 uses that restatement to rule out an endpoint. On the flat slab, h=(t(1-t))^(-2) dt^2+|dz|^2 is complete and proper because log(t/(1-t)),z identify it with Euclidean R^4. Vertical unit-h-speed curves have dt/ds=t(1-t), so unbounded arclength increments fit within bounded coordinate-time increments; no global C on the entire adapted slab chart exists. The endpoint argument can always choose a buffered smaller chart; its geometric conclusion is retained.
